decision: RECEIPT-ONLY NEGATIVE: land no default-kernel source change. The shipped QmmPrefillCoopmatF16 kernel beats every bit-preserving ILP schedule variant measured. Bench arms (4-12), the in-process bit-identity regression test, and this receipt live only on wave/CoopmatIlpChains. Never merged.
question: The 2026-09-11-fma-ceiling receipt showed the 8x8x8 f32 cooperative-matrix multiply sustains 2148 GFLOP/s (93% of scalar FMA ceiling) with 4 independent accumulator chains, while the shipped quantized prefill kernel runs 1032-1043 GFLOP/s at the dominant gate_up shape. Can the kernel's ILP be raised - without changing any output's per-output accumulation order - by interleaving MulAdd issue across independent accumulator fragments and removing whatever serialises them, to close the ~2x headroom?
base: wave/CoopmatIlpChains off wave/CoopmatTflopClose cb6510a6; measurement commits 8c527182 (arms 5-10), ce14a392 (arms 9/10 stride fix), 48ea34dd (arms 11/12). No default-dispatch change on the branch: arm 0 always means the shipped shaders/qmm_coopmat.comp; MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_COOP_BENCH selects bench arms only and is re-read per dispatch.

instrument.what: Chains-in-flight ladder inside the bench shader skeleton at the real dispatch shapes: pure-MulAdd k loop (operands loaded once) with 1/2/4/8 independent accumulator chains per lane (arms 5/6/7/4), every rung issuing exactly 64 MulAdds per lane per 64-k chunk so GFLOP/s compares directly. Zero operand traffic; 16 KiB shared skeleton on every rung (occupancy identical across rungs).
instrument.reference: Hand-written SPIR-V ladder in receipts/2026-09-11-fma-ceiling (flat dispatch, no shared, 128 lanes): 1/2/4 chains = 1690/2003/2148 GFLOP/s. This receipt's ladder is the same measurement inside the real kernel's dispatch geometry (64-lane workgroups, tile loop, 16 KiB shared).
instrument.verdict: The dispatch geometry sustains up to ~1459 GFLOP/s with 8 chains. The shipped kernel's 1043 GFLOP/s matches the ONE-chain rung (1014): although the source issues 8 independent fragment updates per burst (AGX confirms 8 simd_matrix_fmadd32 with dependency spacing 8 per half-step, dumps/arm0.agx.txt.gz), the phase structure between bursts means time-averaged chains in flight ~ 1. Effective chains, not source chains, are the deficit.

schedule_arms.principle: All candidates preserve every output's ascending-k MulAdd sequence exactly (issue order across independent fragments and memory timing do not enter the arithmetic), proven bitwise against arm 0 on hardware BEFORE timing: in-process env-flip test (5 arms x 2 shapes, exact f32 widenings of f16 outputs) plus per-arm host-reference-bound runs through the full dispatch stack, plus probe f16 digest equality on all 8 cells. Gate: PASS for every arm whose timings are quoted here.
schedule_arms.arm8_double_buffer: Stage next 16-k step during current step's MulAdd burst; 1 barrier per step instead of 2; 8 KiB shared. Bit-identical (window A, all 8 cells). RESULT: -43% at large m (gate_up 1053: 589 vs 1043 GFLOP/s), but +27% at 262x896x128 (128 vs 87) - an occupancy signature, not a schedule win. The 8 KiB halves resident workgroups; the 16 KiB chunk arms (prior receipt, -70%) confirm the same wall.
schedule_arms.arm9_load_hoist: All 12 shared operand loads of a step hoisted above the 16 MulAdds; shipped staging and barrier cadence; 4 KiB shared. Bit-identical after stride fix (window A2). RESULT: 3.0x SLOWER (gate_up 1053: 349 vs 1043). Regrouping loads away from their uses destroys the rate; the first window A run timed an unpatched arm 9/10 (wrong stride, digest FAIL caught by the gate) - those rows are superseded by A2 and unused.
schedule_arms.arm10_paired_order: Arm 9's hoisted loads with each fragment's two updates adjacent (2-deep chains). Bit-identical (A2). RESULT: 349 vs 1043, indistinguishable from arm 9 - issue order does not matter once loads are hoisted.
schedule_arms.arm11_register_prefetch: Next step's global loads (x words, w word, scale, bias) issue after the MulAdd bursts and before the end-of-step barrier; unpack/dequant/shared stores stay after it; shipped 4 KiB shared. Bit-identical (A3). RESULT: 3.6x SLOWER (gate_up 1053: 291 vs 1043).
schedule_arms.arm12_prefetch_plus_hoist: Arms 11+12 combined. Bit-identical (A3). RESULT: 3.2x SLOWER (324 vs 1043).

gflop_s_per_arm.units: GFLOP/s, median wall-anchored (time.perf_counter around mx.eval, 4 warmups + 30 timed, honeykrisp device timestamps never used)

findings: 1. The shipped kernel has ~1 effective chain in flight: its 1043 GFLOP/s at gate_up matches the 1-chain zero-traffic rung (1014), while the same dispatch sustains 1360/1360/1459 with 2/4/8 chains. The headroom named in the fma-ceiling receipt is real but sits behind the kernel's phase structure, not behind MulAdd issue order. [measured]

2. The AGX loop is already ILP-shaped inside a burst: 8 simd_matrix_fmadd32 per half-step with dependency spacing 8, 16 per step, no interleave loss in NIR. The deficit is entirely BETWEEN bursts: barrier, 16 loop-carried accumulator MOVs (RA aligned-pair copies), and the next phase's memory segment. [dumps/arm0.agx.txt.gz]

3. The ACQ|REL WORKGROUP barrier drains each lane's outstanding memory before it can arrive, so memory issued before a barrier cannot hide under other warps' math - it lengthens every lane's barrier path (arms 11/12, 3.2-3.6x slower). The shipped kernel's cadence (global-load/dequant/store phase, barrier, shared-load+MulAdd phase, barrier) lets warps stagger phases: one warp's memory latency hides under another warp's MMA burst. That stagger IS the kernel's latency-hiding mechanism, and it is load-bearing. [measured + dumps]

4. Every way to widen the bursts loses to the occupancy wall it forces: double-buffering (arm 8, 8 KiB) -43% at large m; chunk staging at 16 KiB (prior receipt) -70%. At 4 KiB the schedule space collapses back to the shipped cadence; regrouping loads within it (arms 9/10) is 3.0x slower because loads must stay adjacent to the bursts that consume them.

5. Arm 8 wins +27% at 262x896x128 (128 vs 86.5 GFLOP/s): at small work counts the GPU is work-starved, not shared-memory-starved, so overlap beats residency. Not exploitable for the target shapes (262/1053 prefill at n >= 896), where it loses 40%+. [measured]

6. What precisely prevents more chains, named: (a) raising shared memory above 4 KiB for double-buffering collapses occupancy - measured at both 8 and 16 KiB; (b) at 4 KiB, single-buffered staging forbids moving memory across the step barrier (arms 8/11/12 lose) and forbids separating loads from their bursts (arms 9/10 lose); (c) the 16 per-step loop-carried MOVs are driver RA overhead (aligned-pair phi copies, same as the fma-ceiling finding) but are not the binding constraint - they are present in every variant including the shipped kernel; (d) the only routes to the 1360+ GFLOP/s band are outside a bit-preserving shader change: an f16-operand cooperative-matrix lowering (changes arithmetic and digests) or driver RA work that removes the per-iteration accumulator copies.
